Defines: Temporary employee (up to 6 months, excluded from unit); Permanent part-time employees (covered, pro-rata benefits); Tenure (expectation of continued employment after probationary period per COMAR & Education Article 6-201(f) & 6-202); Conditional Teacher (holds conditional certificate). security_nonrenewal_002_evidence: When BCPSS issues an unsatisfactory evaluation to a teacher, and when either the CEO or BCPSS issues a notice to a teacher of re-certification to a second class certificate, BCPSS shall include in that correspondence to the teacher a notice that advises the teacher of possible grievance and appeal rights under State law, the Board’s policies, COMAR, and the Negotiated Labor Agreement.
security_seniority_definition_003_eviden: "System-wide seniority" is based upon the length of continuous service as calculated from the date of appointment as a full-time teacher in the Baltimore City Public School System. Continuous service includes all time spent in the actual employment and on the payroll of the Board including all authorized paid leave time. Time spent on any approved leave of absence without pay or on layoff status up to two (2) years from the date of layoff shall not be considered a break in continuous service for the purpose of seniority status. However, the actual time spent on the approved leave or on layoff status shall not be counted in the employee’s seniority.
security_voluntary_transfer_004_answer: Teachers are given an opportunity to voluntarily fill out preference sheets indicating their preferences, in order of priority, of grade level and type of program, with the understanding that where reasonably possible such preferences will be honored.
security_voluntary_transfer_004_evidence: all teachers shall be given an opportunity to voluntarily fill out preference sheets indicating their preferences, in order of priority, of grade level and type of program on that grade level, with the understanding that where reasonably possible such preferences will be honored.
security_involuntary_transfer_005_eviden: If the Principal proposes changes to the assignment which may include transfer to another school, all teachers affected shall be notified promptly. Changes in teachers’ assignments later than the fifteenth day of August preceding the commencement of the school year shall be made only in an emergency situation. No change in assignment during the school year shall be made without ten (10) school days notice and discussion prior to the change.
security_rif_006_answer: Layoffs are based on certification, qualifications, and system-wide seniority (least seniority laid off). The Board must meet with the Union 15 days prior to finalizing, providing seniority lists, attrition stats, and certification info. Recall favors tenured teachers first (reverse order), then non-tenured, within 2 years. Notice is sent by certified/registered mail with a 14-day response window. Laid-off teachers resume prior rights, benefits, seniority, and tenure.
security_rif_006_evidence: In any reduction of educational personnel necessitated as a result of budgetary actions, or declining enrollment, educational personnel shall be laid off solely on the basis of certification in the subject field assignment, qualifications, and on system-wide seniority counted from the most recent date of employment. At least fifteen (15) days prior to finalizing the reduction in staff, the Board will meet with the Union to explain and discuss the proposed reduction. Tenured teachers will be recalled first in reverse order of layoff. Non-tenured teachers will then be recalled. At the employee’s request the Board shall supply information which will help such employee to qualify himself in another area.
security_recall_007_answer: yes. Recall period: 2 years from date of layoff. Order: Tenured teachers recalled first in reverse order of layoff, then non-tenured teachers. Notice method: Certified or registered mail to last known address. Response deadline: 14 days after receipt. Benefit restoration: Employee resumed to original or vacant position with all rights and benefits prior to layoff, including seniority status and tenure.
security_recall_007_evidence: The right to recall shall expire two (2) years after the date of layoff. Tenured teachers will be recalled first in reverse order of layoff. Non-tenured teachers will then be recalled. The Board shall give each employee notice of recall either by certified or registered mail... employee must respond... within fourteen (14) days... Any employee who has been laid off... and is recalled shall be resumed to his position or a vacant position with all the rights and benefits due him prior to his layoff. This shall include, but not be limited to, seniority status and tenure.
security_rif_criterion_008_answer: Seniority (specifically, system-wide seniority counted from the most recent date of employment; the employee with the least seniority is laid off first), considered alongside certification in the subject field assignment and qualifications.
